#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

DEST="backup-srv:/srv/nightly"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/
scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command:
set -eu
sh -n backup.sh
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$work/logs" "$work/bin"
printf 'test log\n' > "$work/logs/app.log"
cp backup.sh "$work/backup.sh"
cat > "$work/bin/scp" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$SCP_ARGS"
EOF
chmod +x "$work/bin/scp"
(
  cd "$work"
  SCP_ARGS="$work/scp.args" PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" sh ./backup.sh > "$work/output"
)
test -f "$work"/logs-*.tar.gz
test "$(sed -n '1p' "$work/scp.args")" = "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz"
test "$(sed -n '2p' "$work/scp.args")" = "backup-srv:/srv/nightly/"
grep -F "copied it to backup-srv:/srv/nightly" "$work/output"
printf 'backup.sh syntax and mocked copy test passed\n'
stat -c '%a %n' backup.sh
